items.title: Madras High Court strikes down ban on transport of stone and minerals from Tamil Nadu to other States
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Tuesday struck down a Tamil Nadu (TN) government rule which had empowered authorities to ban the transportation of rough stone and other minerals from TN to neighbouring States [Madhu Premnath Vs State]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan declared Rule 3-A of the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation and Storage of Minerals and Mineral Dealers' Rules, 2011 unconstitutional and violative of the constitutional guarantee of free trade. It also quashed a July 27 government order imposing a three-month ban on transporting rough stone and aggregates outside Tamil Nadu. The Court held that the State could not invoke provisions intended to prevent illegal mining to restrict the transportation and sale of minerals that had been lawfully excavated. " Any measure of the State to ban transport of mineral to other States or restrict sales except as provided under Part XIII of the Constitution of India, is unconstitutional and would also traverse beyond the legislative competence ," the Court said. items.title: In the name of women's rights, a plea seeks to limit transgender persons’ rights
items.summary: What does it mean to invoke women's rights to deny an already marginalised community the right to its identity, dignity, and recognition? A petition filed in the Supreme Court by a self-described feminist organisation, Women's Declaration International India (WDI India), has put that question at the centre of a contentious legal battle over transgender rights in India. Arguing that recognising transgender women as women threatens the rights, safety, and entitlements of cisgender women, the organisation wants the Supreme Court to reconsider its landmark 2014 judgment in National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) vs Union of India, which established the constitutional right to legal recognition of gender identity. It also seeks to strike down provisions of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, that enable transgender people to obtain official documents reflecting their gender identity. While WDI India claims that it is not questioning transgender people's right to identify as they wish or their right to protection against discrimination, the reliefs it seeks go considerably further.
